Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 34, verses 1–2:

[It is] Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

{1} {Al-hamd} (praise): commendation for praiseworthy attributes and good deeds. So, to Allah the Exalted belongs all praise, because all of His attributes are worthy of praise, being attributes of perfection, and His actions are worthy of praise because they revolve between grace, for which He is to be praised and thanked, and justice, for which He is to be praised and His wisdom in it acknowledged. He praised Himself here for the fact that {to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth}: dominion and servants, whom He disposes with His praise. {And to Him belongs praise in the Hereafter}: because in the Hereafter there will appear from His praise and His being commended what does not occur in this world. When Allah the Exalted judges among all creatures, and all people and all creation see what He has decreed and the perfection of His justice, equity and wisdom in it, they will all praise Him for that, even the people of punishment; they will not enter the Fire except with their hearts filled with His praise, and with the acknowledgment that this comes as a consequence of their deeds, and that He is just in His judgment concerning their punishment.

As for the manifestation of His praise in the abode of bliss and reward, this is something that reports have repeatedly affirmed and that both the transmitted and the rational proofs agree upon. In Paradise they will see the continuous succession of Allah's blessings, the flow of His goodness, the abundance of His favours and the vastness of His gifts, such that no wish or desire remains in the hearts of the people of Paradise except that it is given to them beyond what they wished for and desired. Rather, they will be given of good what their hopes had not attached to and what had not occurred to their hearts. So consider their praise of their Lord in this state, together with the fact that in Paradise the impediments and obstacles that cut one off from knowing Allah, loving Him and praising Him will vanish, and that this will be dearer to its people than every bliss and more delightful to them than every pleasure! For this reason, when they see Allah the Exalted and hear His speech when He addresses them, that will make them forget every bliss, and remembrance will be for them in Paradise like breath, continuous at all times. This is in addition to the fact that there will appear to the people of Paradise at every moment, in Paradise, the greatness, majesty and beauty of their Lord and the vastness of His perfection, which necessitates for them the perfection of praise and commendation of Him. {And He is the All-Wise}: in His dominion and His management, the Wise in His command and His prohibition. {The All-Aware}: the One who has knowledge of the secrets of affairs and their hidden aspects.

{2} For this reason He detailed His knowledge with His saying: {He knows what enters into the earth}; that is, of rain, seeds and living creatures; {and what comes out of it}: of the kinds of plants and the varieties of animals; {and what descends from the heaven}: of angels, provisions and decrees; {and what ascends into it}: of angels, spirits and other things. Having mentioned His creation, His wisdom in it and His knowledge of its conditions, He mentioned His forgiveness and His mercy toward it, saying: {And He is the Most Merciful, the Oft-Forgiving}; that is, the One whose attributes are mercy and forgiveness, and the effects of these two have never ceased to descend upon the servants at all times according to what they have done to merit their requirements.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 34, verses 3–5:

{3} When Allah (Exalted is He) explained His greatness through what He described Himself with, and this was something that calls for glorifying Him, sanctifying Him, and believing in Him, He mentioned that among the categories of people there is a group that did not measure their Lord with His true measure, and did not magnify Him with His true magnificence. Rather, they disbelieved in Him, denied His power to restore the dead and to establish the Hour, and opposed His messengers with this. So He said: {And those who disbelieved said}; that is, in Allah, in His messengers, and in what they brought. Because of their disbelief they said: {The Hour will not come upon us}; that is, there is nothing but this worldly life: we die and we live! So Allah commanded His Messenger to reject their statement and nullify it, and to swear that the Resurrection is true and that it will certainly come to them. He supported this with a proof that those who affirm Him must necessarily accept, namely that His knowledge is all-encompassing and comprehensive, so He said: {Knower of the unseen}; that is, the matters hidden from our sight and from our knowledge, so how about the witnessed? Then He emphasized His knowledge, saying: {Not hidden from Him is an atom's weight within the heavens or within the earth}; that is, all things in their essences and their parts, even the smallest parts that can be measured by weight. {Nor is there anything smaller than that or greater, but that it is in a clear register}; that is, His knowledge encompasses it, His pen has recorded it, and it is contained in the Clear Record, which is the Preserved Tablet.

So the One from whose knowledge the weight of an atom and what is less than it is not hidden, at all times, and who knows what the earth diminishes of the dead and what remains of their bodies, is capable of resurrecting them all the more. Their resurrection is not more wondrous than this all-encompassing knowledge.

{4} Then He mentioned the purpose of the resurrection, saying: {That He may reward those who believed}: those who believed in their hearts, affirming Allah and His messengers with firm conviction, {and did righteous deeds}: as confirmation of their faith. {Those will have forgiveness}: for their sins, because of their faith and their deeds, by which every evil and punishment is averted. {And provision generous}: because of their goodness, by which they obtain every desired thing, every sought-after thing, and every wish.

{5} {And those who strove against Our verses, seeking to cause failure}; that is, they strove against them through disbelief in them, and by trying to defeat the one who brought them and the one who sent them down, just as they tried to defeat Him regarding the return after death. {For those is a punishment of painful wrath}; that is, painful to their bodies and their hearts.

Verses 10–11: That is, We bestowed favour upon Our servant and messenger Dawud (peace be upon him), and We gave him a bounty of beneficial knowledge, righteous deeds, and both religious and worldly blessings. Among his blessings:

That He subjected to him inanimate things such as the mountains, and animals such as birds, so that they would return (ya'wib, i.e., turn back in praise) along with him and echo the glorification of their Lord in response to him. Among the blessings upon him in this is that this was one of the distinctive qualities特 granted to him that no one before him or after him possessed; and that this would be an incitement for him and for others to glorify God when they see these inanimate things and animals echoing the glorification of their Lord, its exaltation, its magnification and its praise; this is among the things that stir remembrance of God, exalted is He.

Among them: as many scholars have said, that this was for the enjoyment (tarab) of Dawud's voice; for God, exalted is He, had given him a beautiful voice surpassing others, and when he echoed the glorification, the tahlil and the tamjid with that sweet, moving, enchanting voice, everyone who heard him among humans and jinn was moved, even the birds and the mountains, and they glorified their Lord.

Among them: that perhaps he would receive the reward of their glorification, since he was the cause of it, and they glorified following him.

And among His favours upon him: He softened iron for him, so that he could make the full-length coats of mail (al-dira al-sabighat), and God taught him how to craft it: by measuring it in the "sard" (interlacing), that is, by measuring it into rings and fashioning it so, then joining some of them with others. God, exalted is He, said: {And We taught him the craft of making coats of mail for you, to protect you from your violence. Will you then be grateful?} And when He had mentioned the favours He had bestowed upon him and his family, He commanded them to thank Him, to do righteous deeds, and to be mindful of God in them by making them good and by protecting them from corrupting influences; for He is All-Seeing of their deeds, fully aware of them, and nothing of them is hidden from Him.

**Verses 15–19:** Saba' was a well-known tribe in the lower part of Yemen, and their dwelling was a town called Ma'rib. Among the favours and kindnesses of God toward people in general, and toward the Arabs in particular, is that He related in the Qur'an the accounts of those who were destroyed and punished from among those who lived beside the Arabs, whose traces they could see and whose stories people passed on. This is so that it would be more conducive to belief and closer to admonition. So He said: ﴿Indeed there was for Saba' in their dwelling a sign﴾, that is, in their place where they lived. The "sign" here is the blessings God poured out upon them and the calamities He averted from them, which by their nature required them to worship God and be thankful to Him. Then he explained the sign by His words: ﴿two gardens on the right and on the left﴾. They had a great valley to which great torrents of water came. They had built a strong dam to serve as a collecting place for the water. The floods would come to it, and a great quantity of water would gather there, which they then distributed to their orchards on the right and left of that valley. These two great gardens yielded fruit enough to suffice them and to give them contentment and joy. So God commanded them to thank Him for His blessings which He had poured upon them in many ways:

Among them: these two gardens, from which most of their sustenance came.

Among them: God made their land a good land, because of its pleasant air, the scarcity of its pestilence, and the abundance of plentiful provision in it.

Among them: God promised them that if they were thankful to Him, He would forgive them and show them mercy. For this reason He said: ﴿A good land and a Forgiving Lord.﴾

Among them: God, knowing their need for the blessed land in their trade and livelihood, the apparent meaning being that it is the villages of Sana'a, as said by more than one of the early generations (al-salaf), though it was said that it is al-Sham (Greater Syria), prepared for them the means by which their arrival there would be made easy, through security, freedom from fear, and the continuous connection of villages between them and it, such that they would not face hardship in carrying provisions and water-skins. For this reason He said: ﴿And We placed between them and the cities which We had blessed visible cities, and We determined the travel between them﴾, that is, a measured journey they knew and could calculate, so that they would not lose their way during nights and days. ﴿Safe﴾, that is, secure in travel during those nights and days, unafraid. This was part of the completeness of God's favour upon them, that He granted them safety from fear. But they turned away from the Benefactor and from worshipping Him, they became insolent toward the blessing and grew weary of it, to the extent that they sought and wished that their journeys be lengthened between those villages where travel had been easy. ﴿And they wronged themselves﴾ by their disbelief in God and in His blessing. So God punished them with this very blessing which had made them insolent, and He destroyed it upon them. He sent upon it ﴿the flood of al-'Arim﴾, that is, the violent flood which destroyed their dam, ruined their gardens and wrecked their orchards. Those gardens with their wondrous groves and fruit-bearing trees were transformed, and in their place came trees that yielded no benefit. For this reason He said: ﴿And We replaced their two gardens with two gardens bearing bitter produce﴾, that is, a little of the food that did not pleasure them, ﴿tamarisk, lote-trees and a little of Sidr﴾. These are all well-known trees. This was of the same kind as their deeds: just as they exchanged good gratitude for ugly disbelief, that blessing was exchanged for what has been mentioned. For this reason He said: ﴿That is how We recompensed them for their disbelief. And do We recompense any but the ungrateful?﴾, that is, do We requite with the requital of punishment (as the context shows) any but the one who disbelieves in God and is insolent toward blessing? When what befell them befell them, they were scattered and dispersed after they had been gathered together. God made them into stories told about and tales for people, and they became a proverb, so that it is said: "They were scattered like the hands of Saba'." Everyone speaks of what happened to them, but no one benefits from the lesson in them except the one of whom God said: ﴿Indeed in that are signs for every steadfast, grateful one﴾: steadfast in the face of hardships and adversities, bearing them for the sake of God's countenance and not railing against them, but patiently enduring them; grateful for the blessing of God, acknowledging it, confessing it, praising the one who bestowed it, and spending it in His obedience.

So whoever hears their story and what happened to them and because of them, knows through it that this punishment was a requital for their disbelief in God's blessing, that whoever does as they did will be treated as they were treated, that gratitude to God preserves blessings and repels calamities, that the messengers of God are truthful in what they report, and that the requital is real, as he sees its model in the abode of this world.

**Verse 20:** Then He mentioned that the people of Saba' were among those upon whom Iblis (Satan) confirmed his assumption, when he said to his Lord: ﴿By Your might, I will surely mislead them all, except Your sincere servants among them.﴾ This was an assumption on Iblis's part, not a certainty, since he does not know the unseen and no report had come to him from God that he would mislead them all, except those whom he excepted. These and their like, upon whom Iblis confirmed his assumption, he called and misled, ﴿and they followed him, except a party of the believers﴾, those who did not disbelieve in God's blessing, for they did not fall under Iblis's assumption. It is possible that the story of Saba' ended at His words ﴿Indeed in that are signs for every steadfast, grateful one﴾, and then He began anew: ﴿And Iblis did indeed confirm his assumption upon them﴾, that is, upon mankind in general, so the verse is general to everyone who followed him.

**Verse 21:** Then the Exalted said: ﴿And he had no authority over them﴾, that is, Iblis had no power, dominion or compulsion over them to make them do what he wished. But the wisdom of God required that He give him power and enticement over the children of Adam, ﴿that We might know who believes in the Hereafter from one who is in doubt about it﴾, that is, so that the market of testing would be established, the truthful distinguished from the liar, and it would be known whose faith is sound and stands firm in trials, tests, and the casting of satanic doubts, from whose faith is unstable and trembles at the slightest doubt and vanishes at the least call inviting him to its opposite. So God made it a test by which He examines His servants and makes the wicked distinct from the good. ﴿And your Lord is Guardian over all things﴾: He guards the servants and records their deeds against them, and He guards the requital of those deeds, so He pays them in full, complete and abundant.

{22–23} That is: "Say," O Messenger, to the polytheists who associate others with Allah among the created beings that neither benefit nor harm, confounding them with their incapacity and clarifying the falsehood of worshipping them: "Call upon those you claim (zaʿamtum) besides Allah" — that is, those you claimed to be partners of Allah, if your supplication benefits. For they are entirely lacking in the causes of power and in the non-answering of supplication in every respect. They have not even the slightest possession, so they do not possess "an atom's weight in the heavens or on the earth," neither independently nor in partnership. For this reason He said: "And they have no share (shirk) in them" — that is, those gods you claim have no share in the heavens and the earth, neither a little nor a lot; they have no possession and no partnership in dominion.

It may be said: Nevertheless, they may be helpers and ministers to the Owner, so their supplication would be beneficial, since because the king has need of them, they fulfill the needs of those who attach themselves to them. Thus the Exalted negated this rank, saying: "And He has not from among them any supporter (ẓahīr)" — that is, for Allah, the One, the Subduer, there is no helper among these worshipped beings, no minister who assists Him in the rule and management. Nothing remains but intercession, which He negated with His words: "And intercession with Him benefits not, except for one whom He has permitted."

These are the kinds of attachments by which the polytheists cling to their rivals and idols, from humans, trees, stones and others. Allah cut them off and clarified their falsehood with a decisive clarification, cutting off the roots of polytheism. The polytheist only calls upon and worships other than Allah because of the benefit he hopes to get from it; this hope is what made him associate partners. So when the one whom he calls upon besides Allah is neither an owner of benefit and harm, nor a partner of the Owner, nor a helper and supporter of the Owner, and cannot intercede without the Owner's permission, this supplication and worship is misguidance in reason and void in the Law. Rather, the polytheist's aim and objective is reversed, for he seeks benefit from it. Allah clarified its falsehood and nonexistence, and in other verses clarified its harm to its worshippers: on the Day of Resurrection some of them will disbelieve in others, curse one another, and their abode is the Fire; when people are gathered, these will be enemies to them, and they will be disbelievers in their worship.

{40–41} "And the Day He gathers them all together" – i.e., those who worshipped other than Allah and those who were worshipped besides Him from among the angels – "then He will say" – Allah – "to the angels," by way of rebuke to those who worshipped them: "Did these used to worship you?" So the angels will disavow their worship, and "they will say: Glory be to You" – i.e., exalted are You and sanctified above having any partner or equal – "You are our Protector, not them." "We are in need of Your guardianship and compelled to it; so how could we call others to worship us? Or how could we be fit to be taken as protectors and partners besides You? Rather, these polytheists "used to worship the jinn" – i.e., the devils – who commanded them to worship us or to worship others, and they obeyed them in that; and their obedience is their worship, because worship is obedience, as Allah the Exalted said, addressing everyone who took others alongside Him as gods: "Did I not enjoin upon you, O children of Adam, that you should not worship Satan? Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 34, verses 46–50:

{46} That is: {Say}: O Messenger, to these deniers, the obstinate ones who oppose the rejection and denial of the truth and who slander the one who brought it: {I admonish you with one thing}; that is, with one quality, which I advise you to adopt and sincerely counsel you to follow. It is a path that is "nasaf" (a just, measured way); I do not call you by it to follow my words, nor to abandon your own words without a reason requiring that. It is: {that you stand up for Allah in pairs and individually}; that is, that you rise with resolve, energy and purpose to follow what is correct, sincerely for Allah, gathering together and discussing and debating this matter, or alone, each one addressing his own self with it. For when you stand for Allah in pairs and individually, you put your thinking to use, you reflect upon it, and you contemplate the circumstances of your Messenger: Is he a madman, displaying the attributes of madmen in his speech, his bearing and his manner? Or is he a truthful prophet, a warner to you of what will harm you of the severe punishment that lies ahead of you? If they had accepted this admonition and acted upon it, it would have become clear to them more than to anyone else that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is not a madman, for his conditions are not like the conditions of madmen in their choking, their convulsions and their gaze; rather his bearing is the finest of bearings, his movements the most noble of movements, and he is the most complete of creation in courtesy, tranquility, humility and dignity, which belongs only to the most steady of men in intellect.
Then, if they reflected upon his eloquent speech, his graceful utterance and his words which fill hearts with security and faith, purify souls and cleanse hearts, prompt noble character, urge the good qualities of conduct and instill fear of its bad and vile traits; when he speaks, eyes gaze at him in awe, reverence and veneration. Would this resemble the babbling and raving of madmen and their speech that resembles their states?! Whoever reflects upon his conditions and seeks to ascertain whether he is the Messenger of Allah or not, whether he reflects alone or with others, will be certain that he is truly the Messenger of Allah and his prophet in truth, especially those addressed, who are his companions, who know his beginning and his end.

{47} There is another obstacle that restrains souls from following the one who calls to the truth: that he takes the wealth of those who respond to him and takes payment for his call. So Allah the Exalted clarified the purity of His Messenger from this matter, and said: {Say: whatever reward I have asked of you}; that is, for your following of the truth, {then it is yours}; that is, I call you to witness that, supposing such a reward were asked, it would be yours. {My reward is only from Allah, and He is over all things Witness}; that is, His knowledge encompasses what I call to; had I been a liar, He would have seized me with His punishment. And He is also a Witness over your deeds; He will preserve them for you and then recompense you for them.

{48} When He had shown the proofs indicating the truth's soundness and the falsehood's invalidity, the Exalted informed that this is His practice and custom: that He hurls the truth against falsehood so that it crushes it, and behold, it vanishes. For He has made clear in this place of the truth, and refuted with it the statements of the deniers, what is a lesson to those who take heed and a sign to those who reflect. Indeed, you see how the statements of the deniers have collapsed, their falsehood and obstinacy have become evident, the truth has shone forth and become manifest, and falsehood has been defeated and suppressed. This is through the clarification of {the Knower of the unseen}, who knows what hearts harbor of whisperings and doubts, and knows what opposes and repels that of proofs, and so He teaches His servants with them and makes them clear to them.

{49} For this reason He said: {Say: the truth has come}; that is, it has become manifest and clear, has attained the status of the sun, and its authority has appeared, {and falsehood can neither originate nor restore}; that is, its affair has been defeated and nullified, and its authority has gone; so it neither begins nor returns.

{50} When the truth became clear through what the Messenger called to, and the deniers who opposed him accused him of misguidance, He informed them of the truth, made it plain to them, showed them their inability to oppose it, and informed them that their accusation of him with misguidance does not harm the truth in any way nor repel what he brought. And that if he goes astray, and far be it from him, but by way of supposition in the debate, then he goes astray only to his own detriment; that is, his misguidance is confined to himself and does not extend to others. {And if I am guided}: it is not from myself, my own power or strength; rather my guidance is by what {my Lord reveals to me}, for it is the source of my guidance, just as it is the source of the guidance of others. Indeed my Lord is All-Hearing of all statements and voices, Near to whoever calls upon Him, asks Him and worships Him.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 34, verses 46–50:

{46} That is: {Say}: O Messenger, to these deniers, the obstinate ones who oppose the rejection and denial of the truth and who slander the one who brought it: {I admonish you with one thing}; that is, with one quality, which I advise you to adopt and sincerely counsel you to follow. It is a path that is "nasaf" (a just, measured way); I do not call you by it to follow my words, nor to abandon your own words without a reason requiring that. It is: {that you stand up for Allah in pairs and individually}; that is, that you rise with resolve, energy and purpose to follow what is correct, sincerely for Allah, gathering together and discussing and debating this matter, or alone, each one addressing his own self with it. For when you stand for Allah in pairs and individually, you put your thinking to use, you reflect upon it, and you contemplate the circumstances of your Messenger: Is he a madman, displaying the attributes of madmen in his speech, his bearing and his manner? Or is he a truthful prophet, a warner to you of what will harm you of the severe punishment that lies ahead of you? If they had accepted this admonition and acted upon it, it would have become clear to them more than to anyone else that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is not a madman, for his conditions are not like the conditions of madmen in their choking, their convulsions and their gaze; rather his bearing is the finest of bearings, his movements the most noble of movements, and he is the most complete of creation in courtesy, tranquility, humility and dignity, which belongs only to the most steady of men in intellect.
Then, if they reflected upon his eloquent speech, his graceful utterance and his words which fill hearts with security and faith, purify souls and cleanse hearts, prompt noble character, urge the good qualities of conduct and instill fear of its bad and vile traits; when he speaks, eyes gaze at him in awe, reverence and veneration. Would this resemble the babbling and raving of madmen and their speech that resembles their states?! Whoever reflects upon his conditions and seeks to ascertain whether he is the Messenger of Allah or not, whether he reflects alone or with others, will be certain that he is truly the Messenger of Allah and his prophet in truth, especially those addressed, who are his companions, who know his beginning and his end.

{47} There is another obstacle that restrains souls from following the one who calls to the truth: that he takes the wealth of those who respond to him and takes payment for his call. So Allah the Exalted clarified the purity of His Messenger from this matter, and said: {Say: whatever reward I have asked of you}; that is, for your following of the truth, {then it is yours}; that is, I call you to witness that, supposing such a reward were asked, it would be yours. {My reward is only from Allah, and He is over all things Witness}; that is, His knowledge encompasses what I call to; had I been a liar, He would have seized me with His punishment. And He is also a Witness over your deeds; He will preserve them for you and then recompense you for them.

{51} He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And if you could see﴾ — O Messenger, and whoever stands in your place, the state of these deniers ﴿when they are terrified﴾ — when they see the punishment and what the messengers informed them of, and that which they denied. You would see an awesome matter, a dreadful sight, an abhorrent state, and severe hardship, and that is when the punishment is due upon them and they have no escape from it nor any way of getting away. ﴿And they will be seized from a near place﴾; i.e., not far from the place of punishment, rather they will be seized and then thrown into the Fire.

{52} ﴿And they will say﴾ in that state: "We believe in Allah," and we affirm what we denied before. ﴿But how can they reach [faith]﴾; i.e., how can they obtain belief, ﴿from a distant place﴾? Between them and it has been placed a barrier, and it has become one of the impossible matters in this situation.

{53} So if they had believed at the time when it was possible, their faith would have been accepted. But they ﴿disbelieved in it before, and [they] hurl [accusations] of the unseen from a distant place﴾; i.e., they throw, ﴿of the unseen, from a distant place﴾, by their casting of falsehood in order to refute the truth with it. But there is no way to that, just as there is no way for the one who shoots from a distant place to hit the target. Likewise, it is impossible for falsehood to overcome the truth or repel it; it can only have its assault at the time when the truth is heedless of it. But when the truth emerges and confronts falsehood, it suppresses it.

{54} ﴿And a barrier will be placed between them and what they desire﴾: from desires, pleasures, children, wealth, servants, and armies. They will have been left alone with their deeds, and will come individually as they were created, leaving behind what they were granted behind their backs. ﴿Just as was done with their counterparts﴾: from the earlier nations, when destruction came upon them, a barrier was placed between them and what they desired. ﴿Indeed, they were in disquieting doubt﴾; i.e., doubt that causes unease and anxiety of heart. Therefore they did not believe, and they did not repent when they were asked to repent.
